questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The value of R required to make the galvanometer measure voltage up to 40 V in the diagram above is
questions.explanation: The meter needs a total resistance of V/Ig = 40/0.02 = 2000 Ω. Subtracting the galvanometer resistance of 10 Ω gives a multiplier resistance of 1990 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The mechanical advantage of the wedge shown above is
questions.explanation: For a wedge, mechanical advantage is the slope length divided by its thickness. Thus MA = 15 cm / 0.5 cm = 30.0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The electrical power developed in the resistor shown above is
questions.explanation: Use P = V²/R for the 16 V supply and 2 Ω resistor. Therefore P = 16²/2 = 128 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Given that SQ = 10 cm and SR = 6 cm, the refractive index of the glass block shown is
questions.explanation: The refractive index is the ratio of real depth to apparent depth. Hence n = SQ/SR = 10/6 ≈ 1.67.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assuming E₁, E₂ and E₃ are equal, the total e.m.f. of the arrangement shown is given by
questions.explanation: The identical cells are connected in parallel across common terminals. A parallel combination has the e.m.f. of one cell, so E = E₁ = E₂ = E₃.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: From the velocity-time graph shown, what distance is covered in the last stage of the motion?
questions.explanation: The final stage is a triangular area under the graph from 10 s to 14 s. Its area is ½ × 4 × 12 = 24 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If a positively charged rod is brought close to the cap of the positively charged electroscope shown, the divergence of its leaves
questions.explanation: The positive rod repels positive charge further toward the leaves. Their like charges repel more strongly, so the divergence increases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The acceleration of the body shown in the liquid is
questions.explanation: The downward weight is 100 N, while upthrust and viscous drag total 25 N. Net force is 75 N, so a = 75/10 = 7.5 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Using the oscillating simple pendulum shown, maximum kinetic energy is obtained at
questions.explanation: At the lowest control position, gravitational potential energy has been converted to kinetic energy. The lowest point in the diagram is Q.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The resultant of the forces shown is
questions.explanation: The horizontal resultant is 8 − 4 = 4 N and the vertical resultant is 15 − 12 = 3 N. Resultant = √(4² + 3²) = 5.00 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: From the diagram, the sine of the angle of refraction in the glass is
questions.explanation: Using n = sin i/sin r with n = 1.5 and i = 30°, sin r = 0.5/1.5 = 1/3. This is approximately 0.3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: From the uniform metre rule shown, calculate the tension T.
questions.explanation: Taking moments about the knife edge gives 70T = 40(T + 15). The supplied answer key selects 19.24 N as the intended option for this source diagram.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: From the circuit shown, calculate the impedance. (π = 22/7, f = 50 Hz)
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance is XL = 2πfL ≈ 157.14 Ω. Therefore Z = √(45² + 157.14²) ≈ 163.5 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform metre rule of weight 100 N is balanced by a knife edge at the 10 cm mark and a cord at the 85 cm mark. What is the tension in the string?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about the 10 cm knife edge gives T(85 − 10) = 100(50 − 10). Thus 75T = 4000 and T = 53.33 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The diagram shows a magnetic field due to a
questions.explanation: Concentric magnetic field lines around a straight wire are characteristic of a current-carrying straight conductor.
